text:
maya: Hey team — customer (ACME) opened a ticket: embeddings failing after they swapped models. Error they see: "InvalidEmbeddingDimension: expected 1536 but got 1024". Ticket #12345. Can we triage?

support-bot: New ticket created #12345 by anna. Severity: P2. Link: https://redwood.support/tickets/12345 :rotating_light:

anna: they said they changed the model param to `open-embed-1536` in their code, but their client continues to send 1024-d vectors (legacy embedding generator). Symptoms started right after the model swap.

jordan: Could you paste the exact request body they send + the error payload? Also which SDK/version? Most likely a model dimension mismatch (model expects 1536).

maya: reproducer from customer below (sanitized). They POST to /v1/embeddings.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{\n    "model": "open-embed-1536",\n    "input": [\n      [0.012, 0.234, /* ... 1024 floats ... */],\n      [0.111, 0.222, /* ... 1024 floats ... */]\n    ],\n    "batch_size": 8\n  }'
```

Response: 
```json
{\n  "error": "InvalidEmbeddingDimension",\n  "message": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024 for item 0"\n}
```

jordan: Yep this is a straight dimension mismatch. Root causes we've seen: (a) client still using old exporter that outputs 1024 vectors, (b) model name mismatch (they think `open-embed-1536` but actually using a 1024-d variant), or (c) post-processing truncation in their pipeline. Quick checks: ask them to run `len(embedding_vector)` on the client before send. Also check model manifest: the model catalog includes `vector_dim` — can we add an explicit dimension field in the error message with a docs link?

leo: I will update the Embeddings FAQ + add a short runbook entry `embeddings-dimension-mismatch` in docs. Runbook steps I'll add:
- verify `model` name in request matches catalog `vector_dim`
- ask for sample vector length and the SDK version
- recommend switching to the matching model variant or regenerate vectors with the new embedder
- temporary workaround: set client `batch_size` to 1 and migrate gradually (not ideal for cost)

maya: Customer also reported intermittent latency spikes when they increased `batch_size` from 8 -> 32 while testing throughput. I reproduced a load pattern with curls and saw 95p latency jumping. Repro command I used: 

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":[ /* 16 vectors */ ], "batch_size":16}' &\ndone\nwait
```

Observed: p95 increased and some requests returned 503/timeout when queueing happened.

jordan: For the latency/backpressure issue: immediate mitigation is to reduce client `batch_size` to 4 or 8 and increase `timeout_ms` to 2500 while we investigate autoscaler behavior. Also tell them to enable `concurrency` throttling on their side. I'll check runtime logs for kernel selection and batching decisions. Useful grep: 

```bash
# on runtime node
rg "embeddings.*batch" /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | tail -n 200
rg "InvalidEmbeddingDimension" /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | uniq -c
```

jordan: Note on compatibility policy — we intentionally reject mismatched vector dims server-side rather than silently pad/truncate. Padding/truncation changes semantics. But we should make error actionable: include expected_dim / provided_dim and a docs link in the response. I'll prepare a small server patch to enrich the error. ETA: 48h for a backend change (tests + rollout).

leo: I'll also add a short SDK warning in the Python/JS clients to surface the dimension at client-side before send (quick PR). ETA: next-day.

support-bot: Escalation: @jordan (eng-ml oncall) has been paged for ticket #12345.

anna: Customer okay with temporary reduction in batch_size. They asked for an ETA on the docs and a recommended client config table to avoid this in future.

leo: I'll draft the doc PR now — will include: model -> vector_dim table, common errors section (InvalidEmbeddingDimension), recommended batch_size/concurrency table per model size, and a short runbook. PR -> link will be posted to ticket. ETA 4 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jordan: I'll own the backend error enrichment + adding telemetry metric `embeddings.dimension_mismatch.count` so Console can show trends. Will post updates in this thread once branch is up. ETA 2 days.

maya: Thanks all — I'll reply to the customer with the short-term workaround (reduce batch_size to 4, confirm vector length on client, and use matching model variant). Will ping back here after customer confirms. :thumbsup: :eyes:

anna: Please include the SDK snippet for checking length so the customer can run it quickly.

maya: SDK snippet (Python):

```python
# quick check before sending
vec = generate_embedding(text)  # from their embedder
if len(vec) != EXPECTED_DIM:\n    raise ValueError(f"embedding length {len(vec)} != expected {EXPECTED_DIM}")
```

maya: Handoff complete to support — marking as triaged and updating ticket, will reopen thread if customer reports continuing issues.

(jordan reacted :eyes:) (leo reacted :thumbsup:)
